sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Kerrville?
sections.html:
Kerrville is a Hill Country city on the Guadalupe River, and the city calls itself the capital of the Texas Hill Country. Its founding dates to 1889, and the river runs straight through town.

Buyers come for the parks, golf courses and arts venues, and the city names Kerrville-Schreiner Park, Louise Hays Park and Flat Rock Park along the river. Schreiner University, the James Avery headquarters, the Museum of Western Art and the Kerrville Folk Festival are among the draws it lists. Houses close to the river carry both the appeal and the flood exposure, which now shapes how buyers and insurers view the area.

sections.h2: How did the July 2026 flood affect Kerrville homeowners?
sections.html:
The city has a recovery page for the July 2026 flood, and the state governor declared Kerr County a disaster area on July 17, 2026. If your house was damaged, that history will come up in any sale.

The deadline has passed, so a owner who missed it should call the appraisal district and ask whether any late option applies. The city page also lists debris collection, damage reporting through the state and a local disaster relief center. Several riverside parks and the River Trail were still reported closed on that page.

sections.h2: What should I do about flood or storm damage before selling?
sections.html:
Document it, repair or disclose it, and tell the title company what was claimed on insurance or through assistance programs.

  • Keep photos, contractor estimates and receipts for each damaged area.
  • Ask the city whether work needs a permit before a contractor begins.
  • Report damage through the state survey and the local recovery form so officials can track needs.
  • Ask Kerr Central Appraisal District how a temporary exemption affects the value on your account.

A cash buyer can purchase a damaged house as-is, which avoids mold remediation and drywall work on your end. Expect the price to reflect the repair scope.

sections.h2: Who appraises property in Kerr County?
sections.html:
Kerr Central Appraisal District, at 212 Oak Hollow Drive in Kerrville, appraises all real and business personal property in the county. It has online search, interactive maps, a forms page and an online protest portal.

It lists the taxing entities it serves, including Kerr County, the City of Kerrville, Kerrville ISD, Ingram ISD, Center Point ISD, the Upper Guadalupe River Authority and several emergency service districts. Your bill is a sum of several of those, so look at each line before assuming where the money goes.

sections.h2: How do Texas tax dates fit a Kerrville closing?
sections.html:
Value is set on January 1, the lien attaches that day, and bills go out in early October.

  • First half of a split bill: November 30. Second half: June 30.
  • Delinquent from February 1, with penalty and interest.
  • Homestead exemption filings are generally due April 30.
  • Protest deadline is generally May 15, or 30 days after the notice.

These dates come from the Comptroller's calendar. A seller closing mid-year normally credits the buyer for the unpaid part of the year at the closing table.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell fast in Kerrville?
sections.html:
A flood-affected or older house changes which of three routes fits: listing, selling privately or a cash sale.

  • A listing suits a house in good shape on a fair timeline.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale cuts commission and puts disclosure on you.
  • A cash offer works for as-is houses, absentee owners and estate sales.

In a retirement-heavy Hill Country market, many sales also involve a move to be near family, so a firm closing date is often the deciding factor.

sections.h2: How is the deed recorded for a Kerr County property?
sections.html:
The Kerr County Clerk records deeds for land in the county, and an instrument must be signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer.

The Texas clerk manual lists a first-page fee of $5.00 and $4.00 for each added page, plus other records fees that vary by county. The title company handles filing, so ask for the final charges in your settlement statement.

sections.h2: Can a Kerrville seller use a transfer on death or land contract?
sections.html:
Texas lets an owner record a transfer on death deed so real property passes without probate, and a Lady Bird deed lets the owner keep selling or mortgaging the house without the beneficiary's consent. Either must be recorded in the county where the property sits, and the transfer on death deed has to be recorded before the owner dies.

A contract for deed is a different tool. Under Property Code chapter 5, the seller keeps title until the buyer finishes paying, and for a residence the buyer has a statutory right to cancel. Seller financing on a Kerrville house is possible, but the rules are strict, so have a Texas attorney draft it.

sections.h2: What do Kerrville buyers want to know about the river?
sections.html:
The Guadalupe River gives Kerrville its parks and its trail, and buyers ask which parts of town felt the July 2026 flood. The city's recovery page said Louise Hays Park, Lehmann-Monroe Park, Tranquility Island, Guadalupe Park and the River Trail were closed for flood damage, while Knapp Park and Cypress Park had reopened. Repair planning for the River Trail was underway.

If your house is on higher ground, say so and show the water history you know. If it took water, a cash buyer will price the repair, and a listing buyer will want inspection reports. Either way, accurate answers save time late in the deal.

sections.h2: Which schools and districts are in the Kerrville area?
sections.html: Kerr CAD lists Kerrville ISD, Ingram ISD, Center Point ISD, Hunt ISD, Divide ISD, Comfort ISD, Medina ISD and Harper ISD among the taxing entities it appraises for. Your school district appears on your tax statement, and buyers check it first. The Upper Guadalupe River Authority and Headwaters Groundwater Conservation District also tax property here, so a Hill Country lot outside the city can carry more than one special district line.

sections.h2: Does Kerrville have a historic and cultural side that sellers can mention?
sections.html:
The city's own history notes German pioneers and the cowboys who started major cattle drives here on the Great Western Cattle Trail. It also lists the Official Texas State Arts and Crafts Fair, the Kerrville Folk Festival, the Museum of Western Art and venues such as The Point Theatre, the Kathleen C. Cailloux Theater and Schreiner University performances.

Festival weekends bring visitors, which helps a seller who offers a house with parking and guest space, and a house near a park trail will draw people who walk. Describe those features plainly. Buyers from out of the area often pick Kerrville for its mild climate and river access, so mention distance to the water, but also be honest about flood history.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Kerrville house or owe back taxes?
sections.html:
For inherited property, Texas offers a will probate window of four years, muniment of title when no administration is needed, and a small estate affidavit for estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead.

On back taxes, the collector can add up to 20 percent attorney fees under a contract and can pursue a suit. Homestead owners may ask about a delinquent installment plan of up to 36 months where a collector allows it. Call the Kerr County tax office for a payoff figure.

faqs.a: The city's website says the community has thrived since its foundation in 1889.

faqs.q: Is the Kerrville flood property tax exemption still open?
faqs.a: No. The posted deadline was October 30, 2026, which has passed. Contact Kerr Central Appraisal District to ask whether a late option exists for your property.

faqs.q: What damage level qualified for the temporary exemption?
faqs.a: Kerr CAD said owners with at least 15 percent physical damage could apply, for property in an area the governor declared a disaster.

faqs.q: Where is the Kerr appraisal district office?
faqs.a: Kerr Central Appraisal District lists its office at 212 Oak Hollow Drive, Kerrville, Texas 78028. It also has a mailing address on its website.

faqs.q: Can I sell a flood-damaged house in Kerrville?
faqs.a: Yes, either as-is or after you repair it. Gather damage documentation, disclose what you know, and ask the city about permits before any rebuilding work.
